errors.description: The claimed real-vector equation does not ensure the physical phase is constant across codewords, so the asserted logical gate need not preserve the code space. In Eq. (5), for logical zero and a=1,b=0,c=1, the bit string is 0101101; Eq. (6) applies phase e^{i2α} to it, while the a=b=c=0 term 0000000 receives phase 1. For α=π/4 these phases differ, so Eq. (6) does not implement the claimed logical P(α). The issue is that binary XOR combinations of generator rows are not ordinary real linear combinations.
errors.evidence: Eq. (4) asserts that any real solution of Hv=w yields P(α)_L; Eq. (6) gives P(−α)⊗P(α)⊗1^⊗4⊗P(α).

errors.location: Introduction, paragraph beginning “How to execute gates”; Conclusions, opening and final paragraphs
errors.description: The stated code-family assumptions do not make transversal S a valid logical operation for every self-orthogonal code. For example, C=span{1100} is self-orthogonal, but on its code state (|0000⟩+|1100⟩)/√2, applying S to each qubit gives (|0000⟩−|1100⟩)/√2, which is outside the code space stabilized by X(1100). Thus self-orthogonality alone does not support the claim that S is automatically fault-tolerant for the described family.
errors.evidence: “Consider a classical linear self-orthogonal binary code C”; “Using Steane-like code, the logical Z, H, X, S and CNOT are automatically FT.”

errors.description: The printed value of m does not provide a phase grid fine enough to approximate arbitrary angles to ε. As ε tends to zero, the displayed quotient ε/[log₂(1/ε)⋯] tends to zero, so its ceiling is 1 for sufficiently small ε. The resulting dyadic phase grid has spacing π/2, which cannot approximate arbitrary phases to arbitrarily small ε.

The stated gate-count bound O(ε log[1/ε] log log[1/ε]⋯) tends to zero as ε→0, contradicting the manuscript’s own Ω(log[1/ε]) lower bound. As printed, it cannot be a valid asymptotic gate-count bound for arbitrary single-qubit gates.
errors.evidence: The introduction states “at least Ω(log[1/ε])”; the conclusion claims “O(ϵ log[1/ϵ] log log[1/ϵ] ···) gates.”
